name: Lankatilaka Viharaya
description: A 14th-century temple built on a rock outcrop, mixing South Indian and Sinhalese architecture. The white structure stands above terraced paddy in an unusually commanding setting.
directions: About 15 km west of Kandy near Daulagala, on the loop that also takes in Gadaladeniya and Embekka.
tips: The approach across the bare rock face is the frame that shows the setting.
Paddy terraces below run green after rain and gold before harvest.
Remove shoes at the shrine; interior photography may be restricted.
droneNotes: Protected archaeological site — Department of Archaeology clearance needed.

name: Gadaladeniya Temple
description: A stone temple from 1344 built directly onto a flat rock shelf, with carved granite pillars and a Dravidian-influenced plan that sets it apart from later timber-and-plaster temples.
directions: Off the Kandy–Colombo road near Pilimathalawa, roughly 12 km from Kandy. Usually visited alongside Lankatilaka and Embekka.
tips: The bare rock shelf gives a clean, uncluttered foreground most temples lack.
Carved stone pillars reward a close-focusing lens as much as the wide view.
Lower sun rakes across the carving and brings out the relief.

name: Embekka Devalaya
description: Known for its woodwork — the drummers' hall carries some of the finest timber carving in the country, with wrestlers, swans and entwined animal figures cut into every column.
directions: Near Embekka village, about 19 km from Kandy. The third stop on the Gadaladeniya–Lankatilaka–Embekka circuit.
tips: The carved pillars are the subject — bring something that focuses close.
The hall is dim, so a fast lens matters more than a wide one.
Side light through the open edges of the hall defines the relief best.
shootingNotes: Low interior light against bright openings — bracket if you want carving and surroundings in one frame.

name: Kadugannawa Rock Tunnel
description: A tunnel cut through solid rock on the colonial-era line up to Kandy, part of a climb that was a serious feat of Victorian engineering. Trains emerge from the rock face against a steep hillside.
directions: At Kadugannawa on the Colombo–Kandy line, about 17 km from Kandy. Visible from points along the adjacent road.
tips: A train at the tunnel mouth is the shot; without one it is just rock.
Shoot from public roadside viewpoints — never from the track itself.
Backlight from the tunnel makes exposure tricky; meter for the rock face.
openingHours: Viewable any time from public roads.

name: Dunumadalawa Forest Reserve
description: A protected catchment forest on the hills above Kandy, with a reservoir at its centre and a network of shaded tracks. Close to the city but quiet enough for birds and monkeys.
directions: Reached from the Roseneath or Hantana side above Kandy town. The main track climbs steadily from the entrance gate.
tips: Dense canopy forces slow shutter speeds — plan for higher ISO than you expect.
Early morning for birds; the forest goes quiet by mid-morning.
Leeches are common after rain, so cover your ankles.

name: Victoria Reservoir
description: The largest reservoir in the country, held back by an arch dam in a steep gorge on the Mahaweli. When levels drop, remains of the old Teldeniya town surface at the margins.
directions: East of Kandy past Digana, roughly 30 km out. Several roadside viewpoints overlook the water and the dam.
tips: Shoot from the public road viewpoints; the dam itself is a secured installation.
Low water in the dry season exposes the drowned town's foundations.
Haze builds through the day — morning is far clearer across the water.
droneNotes: Critical infrastructure with an active security presence.

name: Ramboda Falls
description: A tall multi-tier fall on the climb between Kandy and Nuwara Eliya, dropping beside the main road through tea country. Upper and lower sections can be viewed separately.
directions: On the A5 at Ramboda, roughly 60 km from Kandy. Roadside pull-ins serve the lower fall; a path leads towards the upper tiers.
tips: Tea slopes around the fall give context a tight crop would lose.
Hill mist can hide the upper tier entirely — allow time to wait it out.
Spray plus hill drizzle means weather sealing earns its keep here.

name: Devon Falls
description: A 97 m fall named after a pioneer coffee planter, viewed across a tea-covered valley from a roadside platform rather than up close.
directions: On the Hatton–Talawakele road, about 6 km west of Talawakele. The viewpoint is signposted directly off the road.
tips: This is a long-lens location — the fall sits across the valley, not beside you.
Tea bushes in the foreground give the drop its sense of scale.
Valley haze thickens through the day, so go early.
shootingNotes: Distance brings atmospheric haze — expect to recover contrast in post.

name: St Clair's Falls
description: Sometimes called the little Niagara of Sri Lanka — a broad, wide-fronted fall dropping in two stages through tea estate country, unusual for its width rather than its height.
directions: On the A7 between Hatton and Talawakele, a few kilometres from Devon Falls. A signed viewpoint sits above the fall.
tips: Width suits a horizontal frame; vertical crops waste what makes it distinctive.
Hydro diversion can reduce flow — it is strongest after sustained rain.
Pairs naturally with Devon Falls in a single morning.

name: Sri Muthumariamman Temple
description: A major Hindu temple whose gopuram is densely packed with painted figures in vivid colour — one of the most visually saturated religious structures on the island.
directions: In Matale town, about 25 km north of Kandy on the Dambulla road. The tower is visible from the main street.
tips: The gopuram rewards a long lens — isolate sections rather than shooting it whole.
Shoes off and modest dress inside the precinct.
Ask before photographing ceremonies or worshippers.

name: Sembuwatta Lake
description: A spring-fed lake on a tea estate above Elkaduwa, held in a bowl of forested hills. The water is unusually clear and the setting feels enclosed and quiet.
directions: Near Elkaduwa, around 25 km from Matale on the Campbell's Lane route. The final stretch is a narrow estate road.
tips: Elevated paths around the rim give the view that shows the whole bowl.
Morning is calm and reflective; afternoons bring wind and visitors.
Hill cloud can close the scene in with very little warning.

name: Riverston Peak
description: A grassland ridge in the Knuckles foothills where the road runs along an exposed escarpment. The land drops away sharply and cloud pours over the ridge most afternoons.
directions: On the Matale–Illukkumbura road, roughly 45 km from Matale. The viewpoints sit directly beside the road along the ridge.
tips: Wind here is severe — a tripod needs weighting or it will walk.
Cloud spilling over the edge is the defining image, and it builds after midday.
Mini World's End is a short walk from the same road.
droneNotes: Knuckles Conservation Forest — check restrictions before flying.
shootingNotes: Sustained high wind; keep shutter speeds up for anything handheld.

name: Nallur Kandaswamy Kovil
description: The principal Hindu temple of the north, with a golden-ochre gopuram and long colonnaded halls. Its August festival runs for weeks and draws enormous crowds.
directions: On Point Pedro Road in Nallur, about 2 km north-east of central Jaffna.
tips: Men are required to remove shirts to enter the inner precinct — plan accordingly.
Photography inside is restricted; the exterior gopuram is the reliable subject.
Festival season in August is extraordinary but extremely crowded.

name: Jaffna Railway Station
description: Destroyed during the conflict and rebuilt in 2014, the station marks the restoration of the northern line to Colombo. The architecture deliberately echoes the original colonial building.
directions: In central Jaffna off Station Road, walkable from the town centre.
tips: Clean modern lines photograph well against the strong northern light.
The long-distance Colombo train brings the platform to life at departure.
Ask staff before setting up anything substantial on the platform.
droneNotes: Railway property; the northern province may impose additional requirements.

name: Keerimalai Springs
description: Walled freshwater bathing pools fed by mineral springs, sitting right at the sea's edge with the Naguleswaram temple nearby. The fresh water stays separate from the ocean only metres away.
directions: On the northern coast about 20 km from Jaffna town, beyond Tellippalai.
tips: The pools are segregated by gender and actively used — be discreet.
The contrast of walled pool against open sea is the frame worth finding.
Hard northern light all day; early or late is the only soft option.
droneNotes: Coastal northern province; security sensitivities remain in some areas.

name: Nainativu Nagapooshani Amman Temple
description: A Hindu temple on a small island off the Jaffna peninsula, reached only by ferry. Its tall painted gopuram rises straight out of a flat island with almost nothing else around it.
directions: Ferry from Kurikadduwan jetty, roughly 35 km west of Jaffna. Boats run frequently through the day and the crossing is short.
tips: The ferry approach is the best angle on the gopuram — shoot from the boat.
A Buddhist vihara shares the island, making it an unusual double site.
Ferries stop by late afternoon; do not get caught on the island.
droneNotes: Island with naval presence nearby; seek local clearance first.
